cards.name: texture8
cards.summary: CorelDRAW Artistic Media Brush stroke (Texture Brush_Paint category). Script render (the .cmx artwork mapped along an S-curve, not a shipped preview) shows a black dry-brush stroke: broken flecks and dashes at the left start, a ragged solid body with streaky edges, separate bristle streaks trailing under the lower right and a split, forked bristle tip at the right end; a fast, rough ink-brush swipe.
avoid: Clean or corporate layouts: the flecks and streaks read as messy; use texture5 or a Bullet preset.

Thumbnail is a script approximation: the brush's parts were combined into one curve with the first part's fill, so overlaps and gaps in CorelDRAW's own Artistic Media stroke may differ from the render.
cards.applies_to: open path or curve: the brush artwork is stretched along the path (draw with the Artistic Media tool or apply to a selected curve)
cards.how_to_apply: Artistic Media tool > Brush on the property bar > Category 'Texture Brush_Paint' > Brush stroke 'texture8'; pick it before drawing, or select an existing curve and pick it to apply. Set thickness with the property bar's stroke width. Script: import the .cmx (C:\Program Files\Corel\CorelDRAW Graphics Suite\25\Draw\CustomMediaStrokes\Texture Brush_Paint\texture8.cmx), size it, then Layer.CreateCurve(brush.Curve.CreateCurveMappedToStroke(path.Curve.SubPaths.Item(1), 1.0, False)); this maps the artwork as a plain curve with no live Artistic Media link (the route the thumbnail used).

verified.note: Full-size render: black dry-brush S-stroke, dashed flecks at the upper-left start, ragged body, loose bristle streaks under the lower right and a two-pronged forked tip at the right end.

cards.name: BulletCurved
cards.summary: CorelDRAW Artistic Media Preset stroke (width profile, .npm). Shipped preview (the .npm file's embedded thumbnail, CorelDRAW's own drawing on its preview curve) shows a dark grey S-stroke with a round cap at the left that starts at full width and thins steadily, still about two-thirds wide at the middle, to a fine point at the right end; a classic round-headed tapered brush line.
use_for: comic and cartoon outlines with weight variation
hair strands and swooshes in logos
avoid: A tail that stays heavy longer: use WoodcutCurved; a hairline tail: use TrumpetCurved.
Very short paths: the profile is stretched over the whole path, so the taper compresses and the shape reads as a blob; give it a path at least a few times longer than the stroke width.
cards.applies_to: open path or curve: the preset width profile is stretched over the whole length of the path (draw with the Artistic Media tool in Preset mode or apply to a selected curve)
cards.how_to_apply: Artistic Media tool > Preset on the property bar > Preset stroke list (a thumbnail list; this entry is BulletCurved.npm); pick it before drawing, or select an existing curve and pick it to apply. Set thickness with the property bar's stroke width. File: C:\Program Files\Corel\CorelDRAW Graphics Suite\25\Draw\CustomMediaStrokes\BulletCurved.npm. Script: the harvested object model has no call that applies an Artistic Media preset (only the cdrArtisticMediaGroupShape type to read one), so apply it through the UI, or draw the same tapered outline as a filled closed curve.

verified.note: Dark grey (#343434) stroke, round left cap, steady taper to a point; measured width at the middle is 0.65 of LineCurved.

review.changes: precision fix from measured width profile; summary: 'still about three-quarters wide at the middle' -> 'still about two-thirds wide at the middle'
